title: Predict a signal's size through fifty layers, then set the weight scale
brief: Compute a layer's gain and the gain after many layers, simulate a random stack, then write the Xavier and He scales and check them on a fifty-layer ReLU network.
hints: layer_gain is n_in * scale**2. The scale is a standard deviation, so it is squared.
depth_gain raises the gain to the power depth. Multiplying gain by depth gives a straight line instead of the curve.

forward_variance: draw h first with rng.normal(size=(num_trials, widths[0])), then for each layer draw W with rng.normal(scale=scale, size=(widths[l], widths[l + 1])) and set h = h @ W. Record np.mean(h ** 2) before the first layer and after every layer. In the relu branch, apply np.maximum(h, 0.0) right after the multiply, never to the input.
xavier_scale and he_scale return a standard deviation, so take the square root of 2 / (n_in + n_out) and of 2 / n_in.
relu_mean_square_ratio is np.mean(np.maximum(x, 0.0) ** 2) divided by np.mean(x ** 2). Use the mean square, not np.var, because np.var subtracts the mean. On symmetric data the ratio is close to 0.5.
